newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 24.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- IMF CALLS FOR EARLY RISE IN UK INTEREST

The International Monetary Fund has warned the UK in its World Economic outlook that an increase of interest rates are needed along with tax increases and cuts in public spending plans. The IMF fears the UK "may be tilting too much towards domestic demand" following the increase of High Street spending versus falling export orders. Unless action is taken, it said, 1998 inflation could exceed that predicted by the government.
-- ACTIVISTS MAY SEEK TO HALT EUROTUNNEL DEAL WITH BANKERS

UK and French Channel Tunnel shareholder activists have said that pending approval by investors, attempts will be made to block the company's proposed 8.7 billion stg financial restructuring. Among details of Channel Tunnel's proposed changes are debt-for-equity swap plans that would give banks and debt funds about half of the equity. A meeting of Eurotunnel shareholders is planned for June.
-- BRUSSELS PREDICTS ITALY WILL MISS EMU TARGET

Despite statements from the Italian government that Brussels forecasts were "incomprehensible", the European Commission has published forecasts that show that given the current economic conditions in the country, Italy would not be a founding member of EMU. The EC list of criteria for EMU includes a deficit versus GDP target of 3 percent, and Italy is predicted to have a deficit in 1998 of approximately 3.9 percent.
-- KOHL'S TAX REFORMS HIT TROUBLE AS TALKS FOUNDER

German Chancellor Helmut Kohl has had his plans to impose new tax reforms on the country stopped by the opposition Social Democratic Party. Germany is predicted to be outside the three percent target deficit criteria by the time the EMU is scheduled to begin, and Kohl hoped reforms could boost investment in the country's sluggish economy. The German Chamber of Industry has called the end of talks between the parties a "shock" and "almost fatal" at the current stage of the economic cycle.
-- DIRECTORS URGED TO CLOSE EARNINGS GAP

The annual convention of the Institute of Directors has been urged to cut the earnings gap between the boardroom and the rest of the workforce. The call was made by Stuart Hampson, chairman of retail group the John Lewis Partnership, and was endorsed by IOD director general Tim Melville-Ross. Hampson, whose John Lewis group is run as a partnership by its 36,000 staff, said the Greenbury report into top peoples' pay had not resolved the problem, but had just led to a repackaging of pay.
-- PIA LEVIES FINE OVER MIS-SELLING

The Personal Investment Authority (PIA), the watchdog for the private investor, has imposed its biggest ever fine as it cracks down on the mis-selling of pensions. PIA fined Berkeley Independent Advisers, a Coventry-based network of independent financial advisers, some 70,000 stg for 'serious failures' over its mis-selling review procedures. It is the first time the PIA has punished a company for its mis-selling review procedures.
-- HONDA CHIEF WARNS ON NEW CAR PRICES

Ken Keir, managing director of Honda (UK), has warned that market pressures will force makers and importers of cars to keep price rises below the rate of inflation 'for the forseeable future'. Honda is due to launch a new generation of its British- built Civic models next week that will cost an average of 500 stg less than the older, lower-specification models.
-- STRONG POUND WORRIES CBI AMID EXPORT GLOOM

The quarterly survey of more than 1,000 companies by the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) shows the sharpest fall in export prices in more than 20 years. Unveiling the report, the CBI expressed concern about the strength of the pound, although Andrew Buxton, chairman of the CBI's economics advisory committee, said 'optimism is relatively high' in the survey as a whole. Pessimism over exports was balanced by a continued increase in demand for goods within the UK.
-- SHARES IN P&U FALL 14.5 PER CENT ON PROFITS WARNING

Shares in Pharmacia & Upjohn, the US-Swedish pharmaceuticals company, fell by 14.5 percent on Wednesday following the third profit warning in six months by the company. P&U said sales had fallen by 6 percent in the first quarter of 1997 and earnings per share would be down 16 percent. The company attributed the poor performance to high costs, currency movements, wholesaler stocking patterns and competition for drugs that have lost patent protection.
-- EURODIS ISSUES FURTHER PROFIT WARNING

Shares in Eurodis Electron, the electronic components distributor, fell 22 percent on Wednesday after a statement by the company that results for the year to May 31 would 'fall well short of current forecasts'. The profits warning, the second by Eurodis in five months, highlights the continuing difficulties in the European semiconductor market. Eurodis chairman Robert Leigh said oversupply in the chip market continues, as do the knock-on effects on other electronic components.
